title: test_role_absent_demand_inert double-frees the trimmed entries array (defer delete + catalogs_destroy)
evidence: core/demand_test.odin:529-538: `trimmed := make([dynamic]Demand_Entry, 0, 4, context.allocator)` / `defer delete(trimmed)` / ... / `delete(e3.entries)` / `e3.entries = trimmed`. Defer LIFO: delete(trimmed) frees the backing store, then the line-526 defer runs core/catalog.odin:982 `delete(cat.demand.eras[i].entries)` on the same backing (eras[2].entries === trimmed). Empirically confirmed by running `odin test` on the package: `+++ bad free @ 0x46D801478 [catalog.odin:982:catalogs_destroy()]` under `core.test_role_absent_demand_inert`; a standalone repro of the header-copy + two deletes aborts (Abort trap: 6) under the default allocator.
detail: The new test frees the trimmed array twice — once via defer, once via catalogs_destroy through the copied header. Invalid free; aborts under malloc, surfaced only as a masked odin-test warning.
recommended_fix: Delete the `defer delete(trimmed)` line — after `e3.entries = trimmed` the catalog owns the array and catalogs_destroy frees it once.

title: W9's `hosts >= 8` growth-placement clause is pre-satisfied by the seed fixture and can never fail
evidence: core/demand_test.odin:615-619 seeds the crowd before tick 1: `host_pos := [8][2]i32{...}` / `for hp in host_pos { topology_spawn_node(&s.topology, host_idx, hp, cat) }` / `camp_pos := [6][2]i32{...}` / `for cp in camp_pos { topology_spawn_node(&s.topology, camp_idx, cp, cat) }`; the assertion at 726 reads `testing.expectf(t, hosts >= 8, "growth must place >= 8 streaming-capable terminals (content_hosts + campuses) by the surge window (got %d) — the aggregation crowd", hosts)`. Seeded crowd = 14 streaming-capable terminals at spawn; 8 hosts sustain 8×1.333 = 10.66/tick ≥ the 9.5 host-share floor and 6 campuses sustain 15/tick ≥ 9.5, so hosts≥8, campus-exists, campus-sources, and stream_spawned ≥ MIN_LAND all pass with zero growth spawns.
detail: The re-pinned test now passes with growth completely broken — every assertion is satisfiable by the 14 seeded terminals alone. The 'growth must place' guard silently stopped biting.
recommended_fix: Count growth-born streaming terminals separately (seed ids are 0..19): assert growth-born ≥ N, or reword the assertion to drop the false growth claim.

title: run_inert discards record_run's returned heap array — 2×4.69KiB leak per test run
evidence: core/demand_test.odin:546: `record_run(&s, ticks, cat)` — the return value is discarded. core/determinism_test.odin:167: `record_run :: proc(state: ^Run_State, ticks: u64, cat: ^Catalogs, allocator := context.allocator) -> [dynamic]u64 {` (returns an owned dynamic array; 600 ticks × 8B = 4800B). odin-test run confirms: two `+++ leak 4.69KiB @ ... [determinism_test.odin:168:record_run()]` entries under `core.test_role_absent_demand_inert`.
detail: Both run_inert calls allocate a 600-entry hash array that is never freed; only a masked warning, but it is new code choosing the leaky call form.
recommended_fix: Capture the result and free it: `hashes := record_run(&s, ticks, cat)` + `defer delete(hashes)` inside run_inert.

title: test_terminal_class_profiles hardcodes the surge boundary (SURGE_AT 1200) instead of deriving it from the catalog
evidence: core/demand_test.odin:445: `SURGE_AT :: u64(1200) // the streaming surge's data start_tick` — a copy of demand.json's `start_tick` 1200. The same diff's W9 test derives it (line 630-633): `surge := &cat.demand.eras[2].set_pieces[0]` / `SURGE_START := u64(surge.start_tick)` / `SURGE_END := SURGE_START + surge.duration_ticks`, with the comment "The window is DERIVED from the set-piece so a future re-tune of the surge timing cannot silently drift this pin."
detail: If demand.json's surge start_tick is re-tuned, the base/surge split silently misclassifies ticks in both ratio windows — the exact drift class W9's re-pin was changed to eliminate.
recommended_fix: Derive SURGE_AT from cat.demand.eras[2].set_pieces[0].start_tick in test_terminal_class_profiles, mirroring W9.
